messages:
vijay: heads-up — noticed jitter spikes on tiny requests when broker prefetch kicks in. p50 steady but p99 jumps ~35ms. suspect race between lease prefetch and coalesce-window timer.

nora: can you paste the stack traces / logs? any tenant correlation?

vijay: no stack trace, it's timingy. repro on unit tests that simulate 4-8 concurrent tiny streams. seeing pattern: request enqueued -> broker prefetch makes a fast lease -> coalesce decides to wait 6ms -> another request races and steals batch slot -> we flush early + extra scheduling hop.

sam: hmm. so two separate systems both making low-latency decisions. sounds like we need a single source of truth for "ready to send" rather than dual timers.

alex: agree. current broker interface exposes `try_acquire_lease()` which is side-effecting. that leaks internal state and forces callers to short-circuit election.

maria: proposal: decouple prefetch from admission. broker provides a non-mutating `offer()` RPC that returns an offer-id + hint. then admission calls `accept(offer-id)` to commit. avoids accidental double-alloc.

vijay: sketch:
```
# broker config example
broker:
  handshake: offer_accept
  prefetch: true
  slack_ms: 8        # jitter control window for coalesce coordination
  max_offer_queue: 64
```

vijay: semantics: `offer()` is soft — it reserves a logical slot for N millis but doesn't allocate GPU credits. `accept()` converts offer -> lease and charges credits. offers expire if not accepted.

nora: I like that. does it add latency for happy-path (single-request)? extra roundtrip?

sam: can piggyback offer on enqueue path so single-request still does one RPC. accept can be inline when we decide to flush. so no extra RTT in common-case.

alex: also add `offer_priority` so tiny high-priority requests don't get starved by batchy offers. priority can be used by admission to prefer accepting certain offers.

maria: second piece: jitter control. `slack_ms` is a guideline coalesce uses to hold short to see if an offer is accepted. it's effectively a randomized jitter + bounded wait to smooth churn.

vijay: implementation concerns: offer churn memory pressure if producers create offers but don't accept. need bounded offer queue per-tenant + backpressure signal `offer_rejected` to clients.

nora: can ops-bot surface `offer_queue_depth` as a metric and have an alert when > 50 for > 30s?

ops-bot: noted — will add metric `broker.offer_queue_depth` and an alert rule suggestion. :white_check_mark:

sam: what about fallback behavior when acceptance latency is high? we should allow admission to bypass offers after a deadline and allocate cold lease to avoid tail blowup.

alex: agree. add `offer_deadline_ms` and a fallback policy: `bypass_after_deadline: true|false`. default true for p99 safety.

maria: testing plan: 1) unit tests for offer expiry/accept semantics 2) microbench harness with synthetic tiny streams to reproduce p99 jitter 3) canary on a small pool with `slack_ms=6` then compare p50/p95/p99.

vijay: short-term quick patch: if we can't land full offer/accept fast, add defensive check: `try_acquire_lease()` returns a churn_hint when coalesce window is active so caller can avoid preemptive allocation. cheaper but hacky.

nora: ok. timeline?

maria: i'll spin up a short RFC doc with proto shapes and sequence diagrams today. aim to implement prototype next week.

sam: sgtm. i'll take the microbench harness changes.

alex: i'll prototype the non-mutating `offer()` signature and the expiry/queue.

vijay: thanks all. follow-up: call tomorrow 10am to sync on measurements. ping @maria when RFC is ready. :calendar:

ops-bot: reminder set for 2026-03-22 10:00 UTC — "broker offer/accept sync"
